newsitem.title: USA: NYS plans hearings on LIPA/Lilco -Silver.
newsitem.headline: NYS plans hearings on LIPA/Lilco -Silver.

text.p: New York State Assembly Speaker Sheldon Silver on Friday said legislative hearings will help determine the fairness of the state takeover of some Long Island Lighting Co assets.

"We have hearings set," Silver said. "We want to know the financial mechanisms and that the championed reductions and savings (of the proposed Long Island Power Authority takeover) are likely to be there five, 10, 20 and even 25 years down the road."
Hearings will also help determine whether the transaction will be conducive to competition on Long Island, Silver said.
"We also want to know there is an openess to competition down the road...LIPA gives Lilco an exclusive for 15 years and that would preclude competition for that period of time."

Key elements of the plan are a LIPA takeover of Lilco's electric transmission and distribution system, most regulatory assets and its share of Nine Mile Point 2 nuclear power plant. The takeover would be paid for through a stock purchase from a Brooklyn Union Gas /Lilco holding company, financed, in part, by a proposed $7.3 billion in municipal bond sales.

Silver noted the Internal Revenue Service is currently writing a new regulation that could introduce a capital gains tax on the transaction. There is no deadline for approval of the transaction in order to obtain a waiver of capital gains taxes, he said.
"We're waiting for the IRS to write the regulation," Silver said.
In mid-May, W.J. Catacosinos, chairman and chief executive of Lilco said the window of opportunity to take advantage of Lilco's tax-exempt status is rapidly closing.

Silver did not say whether the Public Authorities Control Board, which must unanimously approve the the transaction, will address the transaction at its next meeting. The PACB is a three member panel comprised of Governor George Pataki, Senate Majority Leader Joseph Bruno and Silver, the group's lone Democrat.
Silver addressed the LIPA/Lilco transaction at an electric utility conference at the Grand Hyatt hotel in New York City.

Friday's conference, "The Electric Industry in the Balance--The Role for Legislative Reform," was sponsored by The New York State Assembly, The National Conference of State Legislatures and The National Council on Competition and The Electric Industry.
